articles.title: Rochdale's Local Plan for Future Development Moves Forward
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Local Plan, outlining development strategies until 2039, is set for public consultation after council approval. It includes plans for new housing and transport hubs.
articles.content_html:
A plan that will shape Rochdale’s future over the next 13 years has moved closer to implementation following approval from council leaders. The Rochdale Local Plan outlines how the borough will develop until 2039, including the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes to local transport hubs.

The council has refined a 175-page document, which will now enter a public consultation phase. The formal adoption of the plan is anticipated later in 2027. Initially, the plan required that 20 per cent of new housing developments be affordable, but this threshold has been adjusted to 15 per cent due to financial viability concerns. Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that this adjustment does not reflect a reduced commitment to affordable housing, noting that the council has delivered 883 affordable homes in the past five years, exceeding the previous target.

Housing is a central focus of the plan, with designated land for new developments already identified through the Places for Everyone initiative. This strategy, adopted by nine out of ten Greater Manchester councils, aims to construct around 175,000 homes across the region over the next two decades. The Local Plan is expected to attract investment and facilitate major redevelopment in Rochdale, particularly through the Atom Valley scheme, which aims to create 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs.

The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is a key component of the plan, aiming to transform areas around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This strategy includes enhancements to stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a proposed new station at Slattocks. The plan also incorporates improved walking and cycling routes, park and ride facilities, and community spaces, all intended to boost the local economy and enhance the quality of life for residents.

articles.title: Andy Burnham Calls for Deportation of Rochdale Grooming Gang Leader
articles.excerpt: Andy Burnham has vowed to take action to deport Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison after serving 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual offences.
articles.content_html:
A man called Shabir Ahmed, the leader of a grooming gang in Rochdale, was released from prison earlier this month after serving 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual offences against young girls. Ahmed, who was born in Pakistan, was stripped of his British citizenship as part of his sentence and has since renounced his Pakistani citizenship, leaving him stateless.

In response to Ahmed's release, Andy Burnham, the MP for Makerfield, stated, "Like everyone, I want this vile criminal out of the country." He has urged the home and foreign secretaries to explore all options for deporting Ahmed, emphasising that victims must come first. Burnham's comments come as he prepares for his anticipated role as prime minister.

The current home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has indicated she will seek to amend the Immigration Act 1971 to facilitate Ahmed's deportation. However, there are significant challenges ahead, as Pakistan has reportedly refused to accept him back, complicating the deportation process. The Pakistani government has previously stated that it would only accept the deportation of Ahmed if Britain extradited certain Pakistani dissidents, which has been deemed unacceptable.

Burnham's commitment to this issue may lead to diplomatic tensions, as Britain could consider applying pressure on Pakistan through measures such as cancelling visas or halting foreign aid. The situation remains fluid as discussions continue regarding the deportation of Ahmed and other members of his gang, Qari Abdul Rauf and Adil Khan, who were also released from prison and have renounced their Pakistani nationality.

articles.excerpt: Rochdale's Local Plan aims to build nearly 11,000 new homes and enhance transport hubs by 2039, with a council meeting set to discuss the proposal on July 28.

The Local Plan is part of a broader strategy called Places for Everyone, which has been adopted by nine out of ten Greater Manchester councils. This strategy envisions the development of around 175,000 homes across the city region over the next two decades, with Rochdale expected to see substantial investment and redevelopment.

Key features of the Local Plan include the Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy, which proposes reconfiguring land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This initiative aims to create spaces for living, working, and leisure, focusing on stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a new Slattocks station.

The plan also addresses various topics such as climate and energy, economic growth, housing, and sustainable transport. The town centre is identified as a principal focus for regeneration, with recent developments including the £20 million redevelopment of Rochdale Town Hall, which is expected to become a key tourist attraction. The Local Plan is set to be pushed through to the next phase before formal adoption following the council meeting.

articles.title: 64 Rochdale food businesses rated 0 or 1 for hygiene
articles.excerpt: A total of 64 food businesses in Rochdale hold a food hygiene rating of 0 or 1, indicating urgent or major improvements are necessary, according to the Food Standards Agency.
articles.content_html:
A total of 64 food businesses in the Rochdale borough currently hold a food hygiene rating of 0 or 1, according to records from the Food Standards Agency checked on 29 July 2026. Five businesses are rated 0, where urgent improvement is necessary, while 59 are rated 1, indicating major improvement is necessary.

Among the businesses rated 0 are Yo 1 Stop, a retailer located at 1 Middleton Road, Heywood, which received its rating following an inspection on 22 June 2026. Other businesses rated 0 include Apple & Pears, a pub at Andover Avenue, and Wildbloods of Norden Limited, a retailer on Edenfield Road, both rated 0 after inspections in March 2026. Knockout Diner, a takeaway on Baillie Street, and Frozen Delights and Convenience, a restaurant on the same street, were also rated 0 after inspections in February and December 2025, respectively.

The businesses rated 1 include Davids, a takeaway on Dale Street, and Grillo, a takeaway on Heady Hill Road, both rated 1 after inspections on 30 June 2026. Other establishments with a rating of 1 include Denehurst Stores, Meanwood Stores, and several retailers on Oldham Road, all of which received their ratings in June 2026. Notable mentions also include Zam Zam Kitchen, a takeaway on Milkstone Road, and Marland Court, a caring premises, both rated 1 after inspections in June and May 2026, respectively.

The Food Standards Agency provides these ratings to inform the public about food hygiene standards. Businesses rated 0 or 1 are encouraged to make improvements to ensure compliance with hygiene regulations. The ratings serve as a guide for consumers when choosing where to eat or purchase food.

articles.title: Severely Neglected Toddler Rushed to Hospital After Social Services Case Closed
articles.excerpt: A 19-month-old girl was admitted to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.
articles.content_html:
A 19-month-old girl, referred to as Child K1, was rushed to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a recent Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale. The review reported that the toddler was found to be severely emaciated, weighing just 9.7lb (4.4kg), less than half the expected weight for her age, and covered in sores.

The review detailed that the child was severely dehydrated and had no fatty tissue on her body when she was admitted to critical care in February 2025. Medical professionals noted that she displayed "paper-thin skin" and had open pressure sores extending along her back, hips, and bottom. The case was closed despite warnings about a mother's neglect, who was only 17 when the child was born.

The review, conducted by expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall, highlighted that the toddler's mother had struggled with mental health issues and had avoided contact with social workers and health visitors. Following an anonymous tip in December 2024, social workers visited the home and confirmed the child's poor condition but were unable to secure consent for further intervention from the mother, leading to the case being closed due to insufficient evidence of significant harm.

Nineteen days after the case closure, the child was admitted to hospital, where medical staff noted a range of complications that could have led to death if not treated promptly. The findings of the review have prompted Rochdale Borough's Safeguarding Children Partnership to accept the conclusions and take action to address the issues identified.

articles.title: Phil Eckersley Promises Support for Greater Manchester Boroughs Ahead of Mayoral Election
articles.excerpt: Conservative mayoral candidate Phil Eckersley has pledged to enhance support for Greater Manchester's boroughs, addressing crime and housing issues in an interview.
articles.content_html:
Phil Eckersley, the Conservative candidate for Mayor of Greater Manchester, has pledged to provide more support to the boroughs of the region in an interview with the source. He expressed concern that too much focus has been placed on the city centre, leaving towns on the outskirts, including Rochdale, feeling neglected.

Eckersley highlighted the rise in crime in the boroughs, stating that residents are 'too scared to walk home after 8pm' due to fears of anti-social behaviour. He attributed part of this issue to the Greater Manchester Police, claiming they have not effectively addressed these concerns. He called for increased stop and searches and a greater police presence across the region, rather than just in the city centre.

In addition to crime, Eckersley aims to build more affordable homes throughout Greater Manchester, focusing on developing brownfield sites to protect green spaces. He also promised to support local businesses, asserting that he would be the 'most pro-business mayor Greater Manchester has ever had.'

Eckersley's policies align closely with those of Labour candidate Bev Craig, particularly regarding affordable housing and support for boroughs outside the city centre. However, he believes Labour has failed to deliver for the region during their time in control of the mayoralty since 2015. The Greater Manchester Mayoral by-election is scheduled for Thursday, 30th July.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Faces £15 Million Budget Deficit by 2029
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council is projected to face a £15 million budget deficit by 2029 if no action is taken, according to the latest financial forecast presented to town hall officials.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council is facing a projected budget deficit of £15.227 million by the financial year 2029/30 if no measures are implemented. The latest budget forecast, presented to town hall officials, highlights that this shortfall is anticipated due to rising wage costs, inflation, and increased pressures in adult social care and children’s services.

The finance team has expressed uncertainty regarding the annual government funding settlement, which complicates future budget planning. Budget documents indicate a risk that the finance settlement for 2029/30 may not include a continuation of the Recovery Grant, which is currently confirmed only until 2028/29 and amounts to approximately £15 million.

In adult social care, the 'real living wage' is increasing at a rate higher than anticipated, further straining financial resources. An additional allocation of £1.5 million per year has been incorporated into future cost estimates. Overspending in children’s services has also exceeded initial forecasts, a trend that has been noted in recent years, according to the meeting held on July 28.

Councillor Daniel Meredith remarked on the ongoing efforts to establish new care homes and children’s homes, stating that significant work is being done to address the challenges in these services. The council has made savings of £204.5 million from its revenue budget since 2010/11, but the projected gaps indicate that savings of £6 million will be necessary by 2028/29, escalating to £15 million by 2029/30.

articles.title: Three men sentenced for running Rochdale's 'Adam Line' drug operation
articles.excerpt: Three men have been sentenced for their roles in a Rochdale drug line that generated over £1 million a year, despite previous police efforts to dismantle it.
articles.content_html:
Three men have been sentenced for their involvement in a drug line in Rochdale known as the 'Adam Line', which reportedly generated over £1 million a year. The operation continued despite multiple police interventions aimed at shutting it down.

Haider Ali, 34, known as 'The Ghost', was identified as the controller of the drug line. He was arrested after police observed a suspected drug deal on Baron Street. Officers found £1,000 in cash and wraps of cocaine and heroin on him, along with 75 wraps of cocaine and 32 wraps of heroin in the vehicle he was in.

Alan Ronald Ohara, 47, referred to as 'Rocket Ronny', was the driver, while 17-year-old Shane Walsh acted as Ali's lieutenant, responsible for preparing drugs for sale. Evidence presented in court indicated that Walsh had been involved in drug dealing since he was 16, and had continued his activities even after being released on bail.

The court heard that messages on Ohara's phone suggested he was involved in the management of the operation and was considering starting his own drug line. The prosecution highlighted the exploitation of Walsh, who had faced personal challenges and was groomed into the drug culture. Prosecutor Craig MacGregor noted that the gang had previously engaged in serious criminal activities, including bribing witnesses and using violence.

articles.title: Hopwood Triangle Traffic Trial to Continue Pending Township Vote
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has confirmed that the Hopwood Triangle traffic calming trial will remain in place until a formal township vote is conducted to decide its future.
articles.content_html:
A traffic calming trial around the Hopwood Triangle in Heywood will continue pending a formal vote by the Heywood Township, Rochdale Council has announced. The trial, which introduced several changes to local roads, has faced significant criticism from motorists and residents since its implementation.

The measures include the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road near St John's Church, aimed at preventing drivers from using the route as a shortcut. Additionally, Magdala Street has been made one way towards Manchester Road, and new parking restrictions for heavy goods vehicles, along with a 20mph speed limit, have been introduced on surrounding residential roads.

North Heywood councillor Bev Place expressed disappointment that the trial would not end as soon as she had hoped. She stated that highways officers informed her that a township meeting must first vote to formally conclude the trial. Councillor Place is working to arrange an extraordinary meeting, as the next scheduled meeting is not until 22nd September.

In response to the ongoing concerns, a Rochdale Council spokesperson indicated that there is no set date for the removal of the traffic restrictions and that they are in discussions with contractors regarding the situation. Residents are encouraged to submit their views to the council's highways team via email to ensure their opinions are formally considered.

articles.title: Rochdale Veteran Seeks Justice Following Nuclear Tests
articles.excerpt: John Morris, a Rochdale veteran exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s, expresses renewed hope for justice following the appointment of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who supports an independent inquiry.
articles.content_html:
A man from Rochdale who was exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s has expressed renewed hope for justice following the appointment of Prime Minister Andy Burnham. John Morris, now 88, was sent to Christmas Island in the Pacific Ocean at the age of 18, where he witnessed a series of nuclear detonations conducted by the Ministry of Defence (MoD).

Morris is part of a group of veterans who have lodged a criminal complaint against the MoD, claiming they have been denied justice regarding the health issues they suffered as a result of the tests. Many veterans have reported serious medical problems and are calling for an independent inquiry into their treatment. Burnham has previously supported the veterans' cause, stating that there is clear evidence of misconduct in public office. He has indicated that he backs a judicial review into the matter, which has given Morris and others hope for a resolution after years of campaigning.

The MoD has stated that compensation is available through the War Pensions Scheme, but many veterans feel this is insufficient. Morris believes that with Burnham's support, there is a chance for a thorough investigation into their claims. He has said that the new Prime Minister has finally given him hope of getting justice, as he continues to advocate for the rights of veterans affected by the nuclear tests.

In 2025, when Burnham was mayor of Greater Manchester, he expressed his view that the investigation into the treatment of veterans could not wait any longer, especially following the 80th anniversary of VE Day. Morris and his fellow veterans are now looking to the new Prime Minister to take decisive action on their behalf.

articles.title: Baby Found in Critical Condition After Social Services Closed Case
articles.excerpt: A 19-month-old girl was rushed to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.
articles.content_html:
A 19-month-old girl was admitted to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale. The toddler, referred to as Child K1, was found to be severely malnourished, weighing just 9.7lb (4.4kg), less than half the expected weight for her age.

The review revealed that the child was covered in sores and had no fatty tissue on her body. Medical staff noted her skin was "paper-thin" and that she displayed signs of severe dehydration. The case was closed despite concerns raised about a mother’s ability to care for her, as she had reportedly avoided contact with social workers and health visitors for weeks.

The review, conducted by expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall, highlighted that the child's grandmother had taken her to the hospital after she refused to eat. During this visit, family members informed hospital staff that the child was being neglected. Following this, the case was referred to Rochdale's Children's Social Care team, which initially assessed the mother as willing to accept support.

However, after an anonymous tip-off in December 2024 alleging severe neglect, social workers visited the home but were unable to secure the mother's consent for further intervention. A multi-agency strategy meeting concluded that the threshold for further action had not been met, leading to the case being closed. Nineteen days later, the child was admitted to critical care, suffering from multiple complications that could have been life-threatening without timely medical intervention.

articles.title: Failed asylum seeker jailed for bringing weapons to Heywood school
articles.excerpt: A failed asylum seeker has been sentenced to two years in prison after taking a hammer, hatchet and kitchen knife to Edgar Wood Academy in Heywood, intending to create a scene for attention.
articles.content_html:
A failed asylum seeker has been jailed for two years after taking a hammer, a hatchet and a kitchen knife to a school in Heywood. Both Douk Deng, 21, from South Sudan, intended to 'create a scene for attention' to aid his immigration case, Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard.

Deng became increasingly frustrated with the lack of assistance from immigration authorities regarding his asylum applications, which had been refused three times. He was arrested on August 6 last year after workmen at Edgar Wood Academy confronted him on the premises.

A member of the public had alerted the authorities after seeing Deng behaving oddly while carrying a petrol can and a hammer tied to his belt. He was observed walking a full circuit around the school, which was closed to pupils for the summer, before builders called the police due to their concerns.

Deng was reported to be mumbling as he approached the school, prompting the workmen to take action. His actions were described as an attempt to draw attention to his situation.
